00_primary_quality_table: Primary reconstructed schedule weights, before MILP/LP reference evaluation. Limits are logical variables/couplers. Gaps are retrospective distances to certified reference optima; all primary schedules are feasible. The shared baseline is listed once. Full-precision values and reference optima are in primary_quality_summary.csv.
01_primary_quality_scaling: Primary schedule gaps to certified reference optima, excluding MILP-generated contacts. Left: satellite scaling; right: gateway scaling. The baseline is reused. Active resource identities are not fully nested, so differences describe the selected scenarios rather than a strictly isolated resource-count effect. Both methods use the same candidate CSV within each pair.
02_primary_schedule_provenance: Origins of contacts retained in the selected pre-MILP reconstruction, with paired MWIS/COP bars for the five distinct datasets. n is each primary schedule's contact count. MILP is not a category. These are contact shares, not objective shares, execution time or a causal measure of sampling advantage. Sampled alternative branches discarded by reconstruction do not contribute. All seven profiles' contact and weight provenance are in comparison_metrics.csv.
03_terminal_profile_tradeoff: Same frozen 200/50 input for all three combined limit profiles. Left: primary quality gap; right: total sampled reads over all exported alternative terminal branches. Both methods use 500 reads per terminal. Read counts are sampling workload, not total runtime. Both logical limits change together; changing them also changes the decomposition.
04_baseline_logical_dimensions: All sampled baseline terminal QUBOs, including alternative branches. Marker area increases with repeated dimension pairs; dashed lines are logical limits. One-hot MWIS and domain-wall COP counts use common binary-variable/coupler units. These are not physical qubits, chains or embedding overhead; no hardware embedding was performed. Include this PDF at 86 mm width.
05_producer_stage_profile: Shares of four disjoint logged producer phases, excluding unprofiled notebook overhead, sampling, reconstruction and MILP/LP solver calls. Classical producer evaluation includes exact terminal reference evaluation and incomplete-leaf evaluation; it is displayed separately and is not sampling. Recursive reductions lie within decomposition. Nested component/operation clocks are not added again. Absolute seconds are in timing_records.csv; shares do not establish a controlled speed comparison. This is not a complete primary-pipeline runtime.
S01_primary_retention_and_incomplete_lea: Retention is evaluated before MILP: terminal IDs present in the selected reconstruction divided by all sampled terminal IDs. It is not a contact share. Incomplete leaves count all recorded alternatives, not just the selected branch. Zero incomplete leaves are shown explicitly. The shared baseline appears once.
S02_average_terminal_dimensions: Arithmetic means across all non-empty sampled terminals, including alternatives discarded during reconstruction. These are workload dimensions, not sizes of the full unresolved problem or exclusively of retained terminals. Binary-variable and coupler units are common to both encodings.
S03_common_reduced_component_structure: One bar per dataset represents both methods: retained weighted vertices and edge sets are independently hash-checked identical after global dominance. Sizes are candidate contacts, not COP satellite variables. Only the five distinct datasets are shown; terminal profiles reuse the same reduced 200/50 graph.
S04_terminal_and_incomplete_leaf_distrib: Empirical distributions of all recorded terminal and incomplete leaves for the baseline and largest satellite case. They describe bounded-tree workloads, not repeated-run uncertainty. Empty fixed-choice leaves are excluded. Means of sampled terminal sizes alone can conceal large unresolved pieces. Current encodings use one bit per retained contact alternative.
01a_primary_quality_satellite_scaling: Primary schedule gaps to certified reference optima, excluding MILP-generated contacts. Satellite scaling with 50 gateways and limits 30/200. The baseline is reused. Active resource identities are not fully nested, so differences describe the selected scenarios rather than a strictly isolated resource-count effect. Both methods use the same candidate CSV within each pair.
01b_primary_quality_gateway_scaling: Primary schedule gaps to certified reference optima, excluding MILP-generated contacts. Gateway scaling with 200 satellites and limits 30/200. The baseline is reused. Active resource identities are not fully nested, so differences describe the selected scenarios rather than a strictly isolated resource-count effect. Both methods use the same candidate CSV within each pair.
03a_terminal_profile_primary_quality: Same frozen 200/50 input for all three combined limit profiles. Primary schedule gap to the certified reference optimum, before MILP evaluation. Both methods use 500 reads per terminal. Read counts are sampling workload, not total runtime. Both logical limits change together; changing them also changes the decomposition.
03b_terminal_profile_sampling_workload: Same frozen 200/50 input for all three combined limit profiles. Total sampled reads over all exported alternative terminal branches, including branches discarded in reconstruction. Both methods use 500 reads per terminal. Read counts are sampling workload, not total runtime. Both logical limits change together; changing them also changes the decomposition.
S01a_primary_terminal_retention: Fraction of sampled terminal IDs retained in the selected primary reconstruction, before MILP replacement. It is not a contact or objective share, and does not measure sampling workload saved. The shared baseline appears once.
S01b_incomplete_leaves: Incomplete leaves across all recorded decomposition branches, including alternatives discarded in primary reconstruction. The symlog scale shows zero leaves explicitly. Counts are bounded-tree workload, not counts of natural connected components. The shared baseline appears once.
S02a_average_terminal_variables: Arithmetic means across all non-empty sampled terminals, including alternatives discarded during reconstruction. These are workload dimensions, not sizes of the full unresolved problem or exclusively of retained terminals. Sizes count logical binary variables, not COP satellite variables or physical qubits.
S02b_average_terminal_couplers: Arithmetic means across all non-empty sampled terminals, including alternatives discarded during reconstruction. These are workload dimensions, not sizes of the full unresolved problem or exclusively of retained terminals. Connectivity counts nonzero logical quadratic couplers, not physical hardware couplers.
S03a_contacts_after_global_dominance: One bar per dataset represents both methods: retained weighted vertices and edge sets are independently hash-checked identical after global dominance. Sizes are candidate contacts, not COP satellite variables. Only the five distinct datasets are shown; terminal profiles reuse the same reduced 200/50 graph.
S03b_largest_reduced_component: One bar per dataset represents both methods: retained weighted vertices and edge sets are independently hash-checked identical after global dominance. Sizes are candidate contacts, not COP satellite variables. Only the five distinct datasets are shown; terminal profiles reuse the same reduced 200/50 graph.
S04a_leaf_distributions_baseline: Empirical distributions of all recorded terminal and incomplete leaves for the baseline 200/50 case. They describe bounded-tree workloads, not repeated-run uncertainty. Empty fixed-choice leaves are excluded. Means of sampled terminal sizes alone can conceal large unresolved pieces. Current encodings use one bit per retained contact alternative.
S04b_leaf_distributions_s500_g50: Empirical distributions of all recorded terminal and incomplete leaves for the largest satellite case, 500/50. They describe bounded-tree workloads, not repeated-run uncertainty. Empty fixed-choice leaves are excluded. Means of sampled terminal sizes alone can conceal large unresolved pieces. Current encodings use one bit per retained contact alternative.

schedule_gantt_s100_g50_primary_excerpt: Primary schedule excerpt before reference solving: the 15 gateways with highest combined MWIS/COP primary contact counts, ties by station ID. Both panels use the same gateway order and four-hour horizon. Contacts are coloured by primary provenance; grey setup reservations occur only between successive selected contacts. This is an excerpt, not the full schedule. All primary contacts and all gateways are exported in schedule_metrics.csv and gateway_metrics.csv.
gateway_activity_s100_g50_primary_excerp: Primary contact counts for the 20 busiest gateways ranked by combined MWIS/COP counts, with deterministic station-ID ties. Remaining and zero-contact gateways are retained in gateway_metrics.csv. Counts concern the simplified single-antenna, one-contact-per-satellite model, not real network efficiency. Contact minutes and service occupancy (excluding setup) are available for every gateway in the exported table.
